title: Distinct user groups
requirement: Evaluate and claim separately for (a) adults with everyday handwriting difficulty, (b) people with essential/action tremor while writing, (c) people with Parkinson's disease (micrographia, bradykinesia, tremor subtypes), (d) drawing/art users
rationale: Mechanisms and evidence differ; PD writing impairment is mainly micrographia (COR-10)
current_estimate: Groups defined in validation/human_study_plan.md

title: Active correction target population
requirement: Active nib correction claims restricted to writers whose measured writing tremor at the nib is <= 0.5 mm peak per axis (zero-to-peak, DEC-054's convention: sqrt(2) x RMS; REQ-DATA-004) for full correction, with partial correction declared up to 1 mm peak
rationale: Travel +/-0.5 mm; ~30% (15-50%) of ET patients within 1 mm p-p (PDT-12 fit); PD tremor-at-nib unknown. Restated in DEC-054's zero-to-peak convention (REQ-DATA-004); the limits are unchanged, since for a steady tremor peak-to-peak is twice zero-to-peak (human_study_plan.md s3.6: A_pp = 2 sqrt(2) A_rms). 0.5 mm peak is the lower edge of DEC-054's severe class (0.51 mm). Was: 'Active nib correction claims restricted to writers whose measured writing tremor at the nib is <= 1 mm peak-to-peak per axis (full correction) with partial correction declared up to 2 mm'
current_estimate: ET: ~30% fully (within 0.5 mm peak, 1 mm p-p), ~50% within 1 mm peak (2 mm p-p) (derived from PDT-12's peak-to-peak fit). DEC-054's classes at the tip: severe above 0.51 mm, typically 1.7 mm (REQ-DATA-004). EXP-H01 reports peak-to-peak, with DEC-054's classes beside it (EXP-R01)

title: No diagnostic function
requirement: The pen and app shall not diagnose or score disease; health-status data only with explicit research consent
rationale: Regulatory and privacy scope (report s25)

title: Writing altitude range
requirement: Assistance and capture specified for barrel altitude 35-75 deg (nominal 50 deg) at any roll and azimuth; assistance fades outside the range
rationale: Healthy adults write near 50 deg on paper and 62 +/- 7.5 deg on tablets (COR-26)
current_estimate: Design and simulation use 35-75 deg; see REQ-MECH-001 for the travel limit at low altitude

title: Normal force range
requirement: Full function for normal force 0.2-2.0 N (nominal 1.0 N); graceful saturation of assistance above the thermal and current limits
rationale: Axial writing force mean 1.0 N, writer means 0.56-2.08 N (COR-26)
current_estimate: Configuration B holds the design point but not the upper range continuously (REQ-ACT-001)

title: Tremor to be addressed by active correction
requirement: Active cancellation addresses writing tremor of 3-12 Hz and <= 1 mm peak-to-peak at the nib whose tracked frequency is above the per-user gate
rationale: Travel limit (REQ-MECH-001), addressable population (REQ-USR-002, COR-10), frequency gate (DEC-009)
current_estimate: Simulation: no causal estimator helps below ~9 Hz on synthetic writing (docs/sim_report.md s3.2)

title: Grip diameter
requirement: 14-16 mm at the grip zone (0-40 mm from tip); actuator section may reach 16 mm (Rev A bulge 16 mm at 45-57 mm)
rationale: Comfort; actuator envelope (COR-17)
current_estimate: Rev A: 15 mm grip, 16 mm bulge

title: Length
rationale: Brief
current_estimate: Rev A: 150 mm

title: Mass
requirement: <= 35 g including refill and battery, with >= 10% margin carried in the budget until weighed
rationale: Brief; mass drives comfort
current_estimate: Rev A.1 with polymer rear barrel: 33.2 g incl. allowances and 10 % contingency (37.2 g with Al barrel; Rev A 40.7 g)

title: Balance
requirement: Centre of mass within 70 mm of the tip (provisional; ordinary-pen comparison pending)
rationale: Tail-heavy pens tire the grip
current_estimate: Rev A.1 with polymer rear barrel 76.0 mm (Al barrel 79.4 mm; Rev A 80.6 mm)

title: Page correction workspace
requirement: Guaranteed page-plane correction disc of radius 0.5 mm at every altitude 35-75 deg and every roll, after calibration; reduced authority outside
rationale: Brief s2 (+/-0.5 mm per page axis); page-referenced definition (COR-03, COR-04)
verification: EXP-B04 static map with independent metrology
current_estimate: With q_lim 0.55 mm the tilt-direction page correction reachable is 0.39 / 0.45 / 0.48 / 0.50 mm at 35 / 45 / 50 / 55 deg (compliance-aware J, nominal gamma): the 0.5 mm disc holds only for theta >= 55 deg. Typical paper writing is near 50 deg (COR-26). Options: accept 0.45 mm at 45 deg, or raise q_lim toward the 0.60 mm stop (no mechanical margin).

title: Mechanical travel and stops
requirement: Hard stops at 0.60 mm tip-equivalent radius; stop loads limited so flexure stress stays below allowable at impact
rationale: Protect flexures (COR-18)
current_estimate: Rev A.1 mechanical travel 0.60 mm (tolerance analysis); control limit 0.55 mm

title: Moving mass
requirement: Tip-equivalent inertia <= 12 g
rationale: Reaction forces and bandwidth
current_estimate: 13.7 g tip-equivalent (distributed-mass CAD, Rev A.1; the earlier 10.3 g was a point-mass approximation); CFRP carrier option ~9.5 g

title: Axial load path
requirement: Axial stiffness at the nib 1-5 kN/m with force sensing; compliant range up to >= 1.4 N axial; overload stop beyond
rationale: Limit force-induced ink shift while bounding pressure modulation (COR-05). Simulated device distortion 53-59 um at 2-8 kN/m, 69-87 um at 0.3-1 kN/m (results/sim/design_sweeps.json); the earlier < 30 um target is not reachable in the current model
current_estimate: 2 kN/m, preload 0.25 N, stop at 0.6 mm (1.45 N)

title: Pressure modulation
requirement: Normal-force modulation caused by correction <= 0.15 N RMS in 3-15 Hz at the design point, subject to EXP-B08 ink-quality limit
rationale: Ink continuity and feel
current_estimate: 0.07-0.12 N RMS (simulation, literature hand)

title: Pivot flexure fatigue
requirement: Peak flexure stress <= 310 MPa at full travel and alternating <= 150 MPa at typical amplitude (0.3 mm tip), C17200 TH04
rationale: AMF allowables; 1e8 cycles
current_estimate: Gimbal candidate: 177 MPa / 82 MPa

title: Pivot buckling margin
requirement: >= 5x Euler margin for flexure elements under 2 N axial load
rationale: Axial writing load passes the pivot
current_estimate: Gimbal margin 19x

title: Refill interface
requirement: ISO 12757-2 D1 refill; kinematic seat; replacement without tools; neutral offset repeatable to <= 20 um or re-calibrated by a user routine < 30 s
rationale: Brief s6
current_estimate: Seat design pending

title: Continuous transverse load capability
requirement: React >= 0.75 N tip-equivalent transverse load continuously (design point incl. friction) and >= 1.4 N for 2 s
rationale: COR-01 loads at design and high points
current_estimate: Configuration B (Kf 0.717 N/A, n 3.17): 1.4 N needs 0.62 A per axis, above the 0.60 A software limit; 0.75 N continuous needs 0.65 W copper referenced to 20 C (0.85 W at the 96.6 C design coil) against 0.412 W allowable for a moving coil (results/thermal/thermal.json v0.4.4). Infeasible for B as a continuous rating; D (skid) and E (bias) carry the static load passively.

title: Copper loss at design point
requirement: Average actuator copper loss while writing <= 0.25 W (thermal and runtime)
rationale: Surface temperature and runtime
current_estimate: Average copper loss while writing (65 % pen-down) at the design point: B 0.33 W (0.50 W in contact); D 0.05 W; E 0.01 W (results/trade/config_trade.json, parameters v0.4.2)

title: Force bandwidth
requirement: Current loop >= 2 kHz closed-loop; position loop >= 60 Hz with reference feedforward
rationale: Tremor band 3-12 Hz with servo lag < 1 ms equivalent
current_estimate: Design: 2 kHz current, 60 Hz position

title: Local motion sensing
requirement: Housing page-plane motion measured at >= 1 kHz with <= 3 ms total latency and <= 5 um RMS noise per sample on matte paper at 35-75 deg
rationale: Estimator and delay budget
verification: EXP-S01 latency and accuracy vs tilt on paper
current_estimate: Unknown on paper; DeltaPen 24-68 um per 10 ms window on Wacom surface

title: Optical coverage vs roll
requirement: At least one optical sensor with valid view of the page at any roll angle
rationale: Pen rolls freely in hand
current_estimate: 3 sensors at 120 deg interleaved with pivot flexures

title: IMU
requirement: 6-axis IMU >= 1 kHz output, rigidly mounted to housing; used for orientation, contact events and bridging optical latency only
rationale: COR-08
current_estimate: LSM6DSV16X class

title: Stage position sensing
requirement: Lever angle measured synchronously with the 2 kHz stage loop (>= 4 kHz preferred for derivative noise, subject to the 3-axis rate of the Hall sensor, VERIFY) with <= 2 um RMS noise referred to the tip and current-crosstalk after compensation <= 5 um/A
rationale: Servo stiffness and noise; the simulator meets its stability and tracking results with 2 kHz sampling and 0.1 ms delay
current_estimate: 3-D Hall on refill rear magnet (TMAG5170 class) or 2x linear Hall

title: Axial force sensing
requirement: Axial force 0.1-2 N with <= 10 mN RMS noise at >= 500 Hz
rationale: Contact detection, feedforward, gamma estimation
verification: EXP-B05 (axial path against the F/T reference)
current_estimate: Axial slide via 3-D Hall z-channel (k_ax = 2 kN/m -> 5 um per 10 mN)

title: Loop rates
requirement: Current regulation 40 kHz (DEC-012); stage loop 2 kHz; estimator 2 kHz; optional learned predictor 250 Hz
rationale: Brief s5
evidence_status: proposed design; host and QEMU execution
current_estimate: Firmware core runs the 40 kHz current loop and the 2 kHz stage task (60/60 test cases on host and QEMU). QEMU instruction counts: current ISR 422 mean / 446 max (at least 14 % of the 3200-cycle period at 128 MHz), stage tick 11 535 / 13 112 (at least 20 % of 64 000 cycles; 41 % of the ICD's 250 us compute budget). Instructions are not cycles; timing on the nRF5340 is unmeasured

title: Stability margins
requirement: Phase margin >= 40 deg and gain margin >= 6 dB for the loaded plant over declared contact and hand ranges
rationale: Robustness
verification: Identified plant from EXP-B05 plus a loop-margin analysis (not yet written)
current_estimate: Unloaded model: phase margin 35.3 deg, gain margin 10.9 dB (firmware closed-loop test on the simulator gains, results/firmware/test_report.txt) -> phase margin below 40 deg; loaded plant pending EXP-B05

title: Effective delay
requirement: Effective delay from housing motion to nib correction <= 5 ms in 3-12 Hz including servo lag
rationale: Brief s2
current_estimate: Prediction horizon 1.33 ms (IMU 1 ms + half stage period + current loop); delay-limited residual at 8 Hz 0.07 -> delay not the limit

title: Authority limiting
requirement: Correction bounded by travel taper, slew limit, confidence, contact state and thermal governor; no model output bypasses limits
rationale: Brief s11 s12
evidence_status: proposed design; host and QEMU execution
current_estimate: Limiter tested on host and QEMU: |q| <= q_lim + 0.5 nm over 4000 radii; slew <= 40 um per tick over 2000 random slews. ML outputs pass the same limits (guard rules 2-3); the thermal governor derates authority

title: Intent preservation
requirement: Intended-path distortion caused by assistance (no disturbance present) <= 50 um RMS and corner/dot position error <= 100 um on the feature course; deliberate fast features (hatching, fast strokes) <= 150 um max (provisional until EXP-H05 perception thresholds)
rationale: Preserve deliberate features
verification: simulation feature course; EXP-B09; EXP-E02; EXP-H05
current_estimate: Simulation (Rev A, parameters v0.4.4, 12 test seeds): Kalman 100 um RMS distortion on tremor-free writing (55 um on the 4 nominal seeds; both tuning profiles now select the same set), band-pass 168 um -> violates 50 um. Learned TCN 14.5 um RMS but spikes of 125 um at corners on the feature course (above the 100 um limit; ML results v0.4.1)

title: Compliance-aware Jacobian
requirement: Page-to-stage mapping uses identified gamma (suspension/hand compliance ratio) and measured tilt; identification converges within 2 s of writing
rationale: COR-04
current_estimate: Fixed gamma from nominal compliances in simulation

title: Frequency-gated authority
requirement: Tremor cancellation authority gated by tracked tremor frequency relative to a per-user threshold from calibration
rationale: COR-11
current_estimate: Gate tuned on tuning seeds

title: Guided mode capture distance
requirement: Guided (known-path) assistance only within a capture radius of the registered path with user-paced progress; releases authority outside
rationale: Brief s11 s16; HAP-18
current_estimate: Simulator mode 6: circle path distance 443 -> 163 um (results/sim/guided_path_distance.json). Firmware guided.c: template-tracking test passes on host and QEMU. Bench AC-B09-11/12 pending

title: Causal commands
requirement: Every nose command at a control tick uses only sensor samples available at that tick (acquisition time + latency <= tick time); estimator outputs are computed at the tick or extrapolated causally
rationale: A look-ahead of even 1-2 ms flatters estimators in simulation; study L found and fixed two such leaks before its test
verification: Unit tests that change future samples (ai2/tests); firmware replay test (EXP-L01)
current_estimate: Met in the study's code after two fixes (detector window, delayed-ink interpolation); ai2/tests checks the causality of the smoother, detector, learned models, output extrapolation and policies; firmware not yet written

title: Tremor-line gate stays shut on writing
requirement: The tremor-line gate stays closed for >= 99 % of tremor-free writing time for every writer; with it the pen moves tremor-free writing no more than the Rev H tracker + 2 um RMS
rationale: The listening estimator reads some writing rhythms as tremor (259 um on tremor-free writing without the gate, SIM); the gate must keep the Rev H tracker's behaviour there
verification: EXP-L01; SIM stages cl and test
current_estimate: Never open on the tremor-free writing of any tuning or test writer; tremor-free writing moved 26.3 um, as with the Rev H tracker (SIM, synthetic glyph writers). This Rev H baseline is above the 15 um of REQ-RVH-006 and the 25 um of REQ-ML-001 (other writer models). Real writing (study R, HW1 with real inputs, UNIPEN test writers): Rev H and Rev J gated moved it 25 um (14-42), the gate shut 99.8 % of the time (SIM, docs/real_data.md)

title: Gated tracker worth the risk
requirement: At 1-2 mm tremor (6-10 Hz) the ink error is <= 0.8 x the Rev H tracker's, letters read >= Rev H's - 1 point at every condition, and 0.3 mm tremor no worse than 1.02 x Rev H's
rationale: The gain must be worth the risk (study L rules R2 and R3)
current_estimate: 430 against 627 um at 1-2 mm (0.69; paired -197 um, 95 % CI -206 to -188); 6 Hz 818 -> 540 um; letters read 64 -> 78 %, words 49 -> 74 %; 0.3 mm 161 against 162 um (SIM, test writers 0-5, seeds 200-203). Real inputs (study R, SIM): at the severe class (1.72 mm) the gated tracker left 0.96 x and the Rev H tracker 1.06 x of the ordinary pen's tip tremor, with 0.4 of 10 words read for both; at 1 mm 1.03-1.04 x against 1.08 x (docs/real_data.md)

title: Ink lag limits (only if delayed ink is revived)
requirement: Applies only if delayed ink is ever revived (DEC-042: the ink never trails the hand): the ink lag is <= 25 ms while writing, returns to 0 within 5 ms of the hand stopping or lifting, and keeps the hand-ink distance within the usable nose travel for >= 99 % of pen-down time
rationale: Perception: people notice inking lag from a median of about 50 ms (HAP-90); a 100 ms lag cut stroke ends (54 % of words) and beyond 25 ms the hand-ink distance exceeds +/-3 mm (SIM, CALC)
current_estimate: Not adopted. <= 25 ms: -4 % ink error (430 -> 412 um) and no more words (73 against 74 %), failed the letters rule on confirmation seed 301; the command exceeded 3 mm for 3.5 % of pen-down time at 25 ms and 6 mm for at most 0.65 % at any lag (SIM)

title: Guidance fades and hands back
requirement: Guidance level fades across sessions with the writer's own error (forgetting factor f < 1 and a tolerance band), and guidance drops to 0 within 60 ms of the writer staying > 2.5 mm from the target
rationale: Assistance as needed and hand-back (HAP-94, EML-59); a per-letter assistance-as-needed law reacted one letter late (SIM)
current_estimate: Partial guidance (0.5) brought the ink 29 % closer to the target letters (582 -> 413 um) with no loss of letters read (92.9 %); per-letter assistance as needed gave the same share of help (24.9 %) and less gain on malformed letters (0.47 against 0.54) (SIM, passive hand: fading across sessions not testable)

title: The pen writes an accepted word whole
requirement: The pen writes an accepted word only if (a) the tallest letter fits the usable reach (the stage's reach minus a 0.5 mm reserve), (b) each letter is admitted whole before it starts, and (c) it slows or waits when the hand lags, lifts after 0.5 s without progress, and hands back after 2 s without progress or when the hand runs ahead; it never leaves half a letter
rationale: Rule C1 of study S; the review's s10. Reach decides: at a 3 mm x-height a whole accepted word needs about +/-4-6 mm of nib reach with the hand advancing as usual (95 % written in full at +/-6 mm, 23 % at +/-4 mm, 0 % at +/-1-2 mm; 2 % with a still hand), so the travel comes from the hand's sweep (DEC-049, DEC-056 (f)); REQ-RVJ-N01's guaranteed 6.0 mm is the reach that works. This is the plan of REQ-RVJ-N07's autowrite; its hand-backs count in its coverage and completion time (REQ-WP-011)
source: DEC-056 (f); DEC-049; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (T9; rule C1; proposed requirements)
current_estimate: Kinematics only (SIM): 100 completions in 20 test writers' own letters at a 3 mm x-height (median 11.8 mm for the pen to write); with letter admission 0 half letters per 100 completions with steady, slow or still hands and 8 with hands that pause or run ahead, against 2-99 point by point (at +/-6 mm); the pen takes 1.01 x the writer's own time with a steady hand. No stage dynamics or tremor

title: Learned model gate
requirement: A learned predictor may be enabled only if, on held-out participants (EXP-H01 recordings, EXP-E01 protocol), it reduces the residual ratio by >= 0.10 with the 95 % paired-bootstrap upper bound below 0, in each of the 4-8 Hz and 8-12 Hz bands, at matched false correction (<= 25 um RMS on tremor-free writing) against the best conventional estimator (Kalman, BMFLC, scheduled least-squares), and without false-correction spikes above 100 um. Gate fixed before any real data is analysed.
rationale: Brief s12 s17
current_estimate: Synthetic data: TCN meets the gate in distribution (all-band 0.48 vs 0.76, paired difference -0.28 [-0.33, -0.24]) but fails under shift (0.83 vs 0.87, n.s.) and in the coupled simulator (3-15 Hz: 0.73 vs 0.77); corner spikes 125 um. Not met: no real data. Real inputs (study R, SIM): the TCN trained on synthetic writers moved clean real writing 172 um (93-286) and left 0.71 x of the ordinary pen's tip tremor at the severe class (docs/real_data.md)

title: Inference budget
requirement: Learned predictor <= 1 ms worst-case at 128 MHz per 4 ms step, <= 64 kB RAM, streaming state, output with timestamp/expiry/confidence
rationale: EML findings
verification: On-target benchmark on the nRF5340 (not yet run); QEMU instruction count only so far (results/ml/budget.json)
current_estimate: Exported TCN (tcn_s_nofest, inputs dx/dy only): 16.2 k MAC, 7.3 kB weights, 0.58 kB RAM; 0.27-0.86 ms with CMSIS-NN (estimated), 0.90-1.44 ms plain C (115 k QEMU instructions per inference; not cycle-accurate); C bit-exact vs Python int8 on 20 000 windows
trace: results/ml/budget.json; results/ml/export_c.json; docs/icd.md s5 (output carries timestamp, expiry and confidence)

title: Learned estimator on the pen
requirement: A learned tremor estimator is causal, takes <= 2 ms per 2 ms step on the pen MCU (int8) with <= 64 kB of weights, and may drive the nose only after REQ-ML-001 passes on held-out real recordings; until then it runs in shadow mode (computed and logged, not driving the nose)
rationale: Compute and safety; the TCN was trained and tested inside one simulator family
current_estimate: TCN: 34 k parameters, 33 248 MAC per 2 ms step, 33 kB of int8 weights + about 16 kB of history, about 0.56 ms per step on a 128 MHz Cortex-M33 (28 % of one core; CALC, ASSUMPTION MCU model); REQ-ML-002 allows <= 1 ms per 4 ms step. SIM: 278 um at 1-2 mm; tremor-free writing moved 19.3 um on average but 34.8 um for the worst writer (above REQ-ML-001's 25 um)

title: RL arbitration gate
requirement: No RL policy drives the nose (DEC-042). An RL policy may arbitrate assistance on the pen only if, in closed loop on held-out writers and seeds, it meets REQ-CTRL-010 and REQ-CTRL-011 and beats the model-based gate by >= 5 %
rationale: Replay rewards did not predict closed-loop false correction (SIM)
current_estimate: Replay-trained PPO arbiter: 298 um and 89 % of words at 1-2 mm, but tremor-free writing moved 30.7 um (60.9 um on tuning) and worse than Rev H at 10 Hz, 0.3 mm: fails rules R1 and R2; residual RL moved tremor-free writing by 165 um (SIM). No closed-loop training yet

title: Runtime
requirement: >= 60 min active writing at the design point with the qualified cell
rationale: Brief s2
verification: power budget; EXP-P01 (measured power and duty cycle)
current_estimate: B: 81 min writing at 65 % pen-down duty (54 min continuous contact) at the design point; D: 215 min; E: 277 min (200 mAh x 0.8 usable, 115 mW electronics; results/trade/config_trade.json v0.4.2)

title: Cell current capability
requirement: Cell rated for >= 2 A pulse and >= 1 A continuous with protection IC
rationale: Actuator peaks (COR-14)
verification: EXP-P02 (cell qualification, charging and battery safety pre-compliance)
current_estimate: Peak cell current ~0.8 A (2 coils + electronics) -> pouch rated >= 5 C; 10440 cells limited to ~1 C (COR-14)

title: Actuation during charging
requirement: Actuation disabled while charging in research builds
rationale: Brief s10
evidence_status: proposed design; host and QEMU execution
current_estimate: Hardware: ACT_EN = REQ.FAULT_N.NOCHG removes VMOT while charging (schematic). Firmware: system test (e) passes on host and QEMU; actuation is off while charging and re-arming is refused until unplug

title: Touch temperature
requirement: Continuously held surfaces <= 43 C absolute in a rated maximum room of 30 C, that is <= 13 K above the room (ECMA-287 B.5), with 41 C (11 K) as the design target; on the Rev J pen checked at the web over the coil plate
rationale: ECMA-287 Table 5.2: continuously held parts, all materials, 43 C (from EN 563; continuous holding below 8 h); its B.5 lets the maker rate a room above 25 C, and the check becomes T - T_room <= 43 - T_rated; IEC 60601-1: 41 C needs no justification. One rule for every held surface (DEC-045). Was: <= 41 C design target, 43 C absolute at 25 C ambient (provisional; regulatory review)
verification: thermal model; EXP-B07; EXP-D06; EXP-J13 (the web, Rev J.1)
current_estimate: See results/thermal. Rev J.1 (DEC-045): the web over the coil plate 35.9 C at 1 mm tremor in a 30 C room with the 0.1 mm graphite sheet in the shell wall; autowrite with 2 mm tremor 43.7 C (CALC, fin model); suspended by DEC-046 (the static side load of REQ-RVJ-N10 is not in it)

title: Coil temperature
requirement: Coil hot-spot <= 120 C (class B margin) including moving-coil air-gap resistance
rationale: Magnet demagnetisation and insulation
current_estimate: Moving coil 96.6 C at the design load, 65 % pen-down (thermal network v0.4.4, 0.50 mm air gaps); the 120 C limit sets the 0.412 W allowable; overload (2 N, 35 deg) reaches 120 C in about 17 s without derating (one-node extrapolation of F5)

title: Independent actuator disable
requirement: Hardware disable of both bridges independent of firmware on over-current, over-temperature or watchdog
rationale: Brief s9
current_estimate: Hardware AND gate ACT_EN = REQ.FAULT_N.NOCHG on the load switch (schematic sheet fault_handling); ngspice: trip 8.8 us, VMOT off 22.6 us after a coil short. Firmware host test of the latch model: it clears only with ACT_EN_REQ low and is declared FAILED after 3 retries

title: Current limits
requirement: Software limit 0.60 A per axis; independent hardware trip at +/-0.80 A
rationale: Thermal and cell
current_estimate: Software limit 0.60 A per axis; independent window-comparator latch at +/-0.80 A

title: Stale or invalid model output
requirement: Expired, NaN, saturated or low-confidence model outputs reduce authority smoothly within 20 ms and never exceed deterministic limits
rationale: Brief s15
verification: unit tests with injected faults; EXP-F02
evidence_status: proposed design; host and QEMU execution
current_estimate:
Guard v1.2 in firmware:
- NaN/Inf and int16 output saturation are rejected at the next 2 kHz tick, and outputs expire at t_acq + 8 ms.
- On running-RMS inconsistency the guard falls back to the Kalman estimate 38.5 ms after a bad predictor starts; the Kalman is fully in use 20 ms later, and the predictor is re-admitted after at least 1 s.
- Confidence rule (5) normalises to byte/255 and slews over 20 ms.
Tested on host and QEMU with injected good, bad, NaN, saturated, stale and low-confidence predictors

title: Power-loss behaviour
requirement: On brown-out or fault during contact, ramp actuator current down over >= 30 ms using hold-up energy; document the resulting mark length; controlled shutdown preferred at lift
rationale: COR-19
current_estimate: Simulated power loss in contact moves the ink up to ~0.8 mm within 50 ms (F3). The firmware state machine implements the rule: low-battery and thermal faults hold neutral in contact and de-energise only after pen-up or a 5 s timeout. System fault sequences (b) and (c) pass on host and QEMU

title: Original stroke record
requirement: Immutable timestamped record of estimated nib page position incl. measured nib offset, uncertainty, contact, force, calibration and firmware/model versions
rationale: Brief s5 s16
current_estimate: ICD v1 stroke sample lacks nib-offset and uncertainty fields (planned for v2, docs/icd.md s4.6); format error RMS 3.6 um, max 120.6 um (81.5 um with pen-down/up samples; results/app/capture_fidelity.json)

title: Offline buffering and recovery
requirement: Local capture continues without phone; append-only blocks with CRC; power loss loses <= 1 block; sync idempotent; storage-full never silently deletes unsynced pages
rationale: Brief s2 s16
current_estimate: Record framing with CRC-16 and resynchronisation is implemented and tested (firmware log_format.c; the app reader resyncs after corruption; golden log round-trips byte-identically). Not implemented: flash block storage, power-loss behaviour, sync and the storage-full policy, because no flash or BLE driver exists yet

title: Page identity
requirement: Research builds use coded paper or external reference for absolute pose; ordinary-paper relocalisation treated as research risk
rationale: COR-16; OPT findings
current_estimate: Ncode/Anoto licensing costs noted

title: Recognition
requirement: On-device recogniser evaluated on target users before adoption; alternatives preserved; recognised text linked to stroke IDs
rationale: Brief s16
current_estimate: ML Kit default candidate

title: Grounded note assistance
requirement: Every extracted fact or answer cites source stroke regions; uncertain names, numbers and dates shown with original ink; cloud use explicit
rationale: Brief s16

title: Useful text suggestions
requirement: Next-word or word-completion suggestions reach >= 30 % top-3 accuracy on the user's own notes before they are shown by default, at <= 20 ms per suggestion on the phone
rationale: Weak suggestions cost more than they save (EML-63); here 18-28 % top-3 before the first letter (CALC)
verification: EXP-L06; EXP-S14 (the personalised model over 4 weeks); CALC
current_estimate: Next word before its first letter: 9-15 % top-1 and 18-28 % top-3 for every model (below 30 %); word completion after the first letters not yet measured. Per query on the study's CPU (one shared thread): next word 1.1 ms (larger-corpus n-gram) and 115 ms (mixture), letter two ahead 34 and 74 ms (CALC); phone not measured. Study S (CALC on two public-domain journals standing in for notes): word completion after one letter 52-56 % top-3 with the personalised model and 46-47 % with NG0, 2.2-3.0 ms at the 95th percentile on the study's CPU; the next word before its first letter 22-24 %: completions meet the line, next words do not (docs/spelling_and_clarity.md T4)

title: Synthetic handwriting labelled and legible
requirement: Synthesised handwriting is always labelled as synthetic, and is legible to the app's recogniser for >= 95 % of letters
rationale: Honesty; usefulness (96 % here, CALC); immutable originals and provenance (DEC-017)
current_estimate: Sigma-lognormal synthesis from 1 or 3 of the writer's own letters: 96 % legible to the app's recogniser; writer identified among six in 92-96 % of cases on synthetic, font-based writers, which flatters identification (CALC); the spread-tuning rule Y1 failed (the perturbation costs legibility on some letters)

title: Ink record, transcript and writing plan kept apart
requirement: The ink record, the transcript and the pen's writing plan are separate stores: the ink record is append-only and verifiable; every transcript change is logged and can be undone; a writing plan exists only for text the writer accepted
rationale: The independent review (s10), adopted by study S (DEC-056 (a), (f)). Permanent ink cannot be corrected by moving the nib, so the record of what the pen did on each stroke (nothing, nudged, withheld ink, wrote an accepted word) must never change afterwards, and what the app reads must stay apart from what the writer decides the text should say. It extends REQ-PNC-008 (autocorrect only in a derived layer) and DEC-017 (immutable originals and provenance) to the pen's writing plan
source: DEC-056; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (the three outputs; proposed requirements); independent review 2026-09-29 s10
verification: ai3/tests/test_layers.py; the demo's smoke test; code review of the firmware and app; EXP-S18 (AC-S18-04)
current_estimate: ai3/layers.py specifies the three stores (StrokeRecord, Transcript, WritingPlan); its tests check the append-only, hash-chained record and tamper detection, the audited and undoable transcript, protected words never flagged, the auto mode only when opted in and confident, plans only from a writer's acceptance, and plans that a new prediction cannot change; the prototype page passes 28 of 28 smoke-test checks (test). Not yet in the pen's firmware or the app

title: Recognition reported before spelling cues
requirement: Recognition is reported as CER and WER on held-out people and held-out sessions, with and without the language model, before any spelling cue is on by default
rationale: Recognition is the weak link of spelling help: when the pen reads the letters itself, recognition errors look like misspellings (with raw recognised letters, mid-word cues fired about 40 times per 100 correct words, SIM). The review's gate G7. It extends REQ-APP-001 (the recogniser evaluated on target users before adoption; EXP-C01 tests the app's default recogniser) to the pen's own streaming recogniser, with sessions held out as well as people (REQ-DATA-001). DEC-056 is revisited if more than 20 % of words are read wrong (EXP-S17)
source: DEC-056; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (T7; proposed requirements); independent review 2026-09-29 (G7)
verification: EXP-S17 (AC-S17-01; the accuracy lines AC-S17-02, AC-S17-03)
current_estimate: SIM on real letters of 20 held-out UJI writers, words assembled with ASSUMED print spacing: CER 9.1 % and WER 19.8 % with the language model, 22.9 % and 54.7 % without (writer-disjoint); calibrated on the writer's other session 9.2 % and 20.2 % (session-disjoint); tight spacing 10.5 % and 22.5 %. Joined-up writing and the pen's own recordings not yet tested (EXP-S17)

title: Spelling help: few false alarms, calibrated, abstains
requirement: Spelling help: <= 2 false alarms per 100 correct words; names, numbers and words the writer marks are never flagged; P(misspelled) is calibrated, with ECE <= 0.05 on held-out users; below the threshold it abstains; in the opt-in automatic mode <= 0.5 correct words are changed per 100
rationale: DEC-056 (c): the pen should ask, not act, at today's reading accuracy (study S, T8). Names were the commonest false alarm (12 of 43 on 4 tuning children, rule S2). Relation: REQ-PNC-008 and EXP-A03 (autocorrect of recognition errors in a derived layer, posterior >= 0.9 by default; AC-A03-02 allows 0.1 % of correctly recognised words changed, upper bound 0.5 %) cover the app's autocorrect; this requirement covers spelling help, whose opt-in automatic mode is judged per 100 correct words
source: DEC-056; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (T2, T8; rules S2, W2-W5; proposed requirements)
verification: EXP-S12 (AC-S12-02); EXP-S20 (AC-S20-01); EXP-S18 (the automatic mode, AC-S18-03)
current_estimate: Letters known exactly: 63 % of 11 test children's real misspellings caught at 2.3 false alarms per 100 correct words (CALC; the rule aimed at 2 and got 1.7 on the tuning children). The pen's own reading: 34 % caught at 1.7 per 100 (new writer) and 28 % at 2.3 (calibrated); ECE 0.06-0.08 raw and 0.03 after Platt scaling; the opt-in automatic mode changed no correct word and fixed almost nothing (SIM; post-hoc rule W5, to confirm in EXP-S20)

title: Suggestions only at natural pauses
requirement: Suggestions and completions are offered only at natural pauses (no pop-up while a letter is being written), at most 3 at a time, accepted with one accessible action (tap, key or pen gesture), and optionally read aloud
rationale: DEC-056 (d), (e); the review's R20 (accuracy against fluency). A tick at the next pause with up to 3 suggestions fixed 3.0 of 10 misspellings on paper with no cue while a word was being written, against 3.4 for a tick plus a pen lift with 7.7 cues felt mid-word per 100 words (SIM, writer responses ASSUMED); EXP-S18 compares them with writers. Weak suggestions cost more than they save (LIT EML-63; REQ-APP-003)
source: DEC-056; docs/spelling_and_clarity.md (T3, T4; rules S4, P2, I1; proposed requirements)
verification: EXP-S18 (AC-S18-05; the comparison AC-S18-01); app design review
current_estimate: Tick at the next pause with up to 3 suggestions: 3.0 of 10 misspellings fixed on paper (1.6-4.0 over the assumed responses), 6.4 suggestion lists read per 100 words, +17 % writing time (SIM, 11 test children's real errors). The prototype page offers completions at pauses (28 of 28 smoke-test checks)

title: Splits
requirement: Splits by participant and session before windowing; held-out devices/refills/papers for generalisation tests; seeds recorded
rationale: Brief s13
current_estimate: Implemented for synthetic writers in ml/datasets.py; participant/session splits apply to EXP-H01 data

title: Real inputs for every writing claim
requirement: Every tracker or pen claim about writing is also evaluated on real recorded writing and real recorded tremor (the realdata library or better), on test writers and test subjects only, and reported next to the synthetic result as a results card: words read by a literal reader out of 10, tremor left at the tip in mm, and how much clean writing changed (DEC-054)
rationale: The synthetic writers and tremor model differ from real ones in ways that change the results: at 1 mm the Rev J gated tracker left 0.68 x the ordinary pen's tip tremor with synthetic writing and tremor, 0.72 x with real writing, 1.03 x with real tremor as well and 1.04 x with the DeltaPen-class page sensor; the TCN 0.36 -> 0.54 -> 0.82 -> 0.83 x (SIM, docs/real_data.md, the bridge). Results on synthetic writers or tremor are labelled as model-input results (DEC-054). At the severe class a legibility claim needs DEC-055's pass line (AC-R02-01)
source: DEC-054; DEC-055; docs/real_data.md (proposed requirements; the bridge)
verification: results card with both input sets (EXP-R02: AC-R02-01, AC-R02-02)
current_estimate: Severe class (1.72 mm at the tip), real inputs, readable words out of 10: ordinary pen 0.5, Rev H 0.4, Rev J gated 0.4, TCN 0.2; perfect knowledge 7.0; the same notes without tremor 6.8 (SIM, 9 test writers, PD and ET pooled). The earlier headline on synthetic inputs: Rev J gated cut the ink error at 1-2 mm from 830 to 430 um, and 74 % of words were read instead of 31 % (SIM, results/ai2/ai2.json)

title: Clean writing for false correction
requirement: False correction ('clean writing changed') on real writing is measured on real tremor-free writing recorded on paper with a clean digitiser: <= 2.5 % of its pen-down velocity energy at 8-12 Hz, checked with sim2j.writers.kinematics before use
rationale: BRUSH's timing artefact (35.6 % of its pen-down velocity energy at 8-12 Hz) made the trackers move clean ink by 160-880 um; real writing on paper carries 1.3-1.7 % (LIT CON-25). This requirement sets the writing on which false correction is measured, not its limit. The limits stay: on real writing the absolute 25 um of the false-correction convention (validation/README.md s2; AC-E01-09, REQ-ML-001, and DEC-055's line); in sim2 REQ-RVJ-C02 (25 um against the device-off pen); REQ-CTRL-010's relative bound (Rev H + 2 um) only for HW1 on synthetic writers. Study R's selection rule also asks <= 3 % above 12 Hz, 15-60 mm/s and writing on paper
source: DEC-054; DEC-055; docs/real_data.md (the writing library); LIT CON-25
verification: kinematics check before use (realdata.kinematics; EXP-R02, AC-R02-03)
current_estimate: UNIPEN hpb2 (ballpoint on paper, 100 samples/s) 2.4 % and UCI Character Trajectories 1.3 % pass; BRUSH 35.6 % and the synthetic writers 10.1-17.3 % fail (CALC on DATA)

title: Tremor class in mm at the tip
requirement: Claims name the tremor class in mm at the pen tip (peak = sqrt(2) x RMS of the major axis in f0 +/- 2 Hz; DEC-054's classes: mild 0.03-0.16 mm, moderate 0.16-0.51 mm, severe above 0.51 mm, typically 1.7 mm) and the population, never 'tremor' alone
rationale: The data's severe class starts at about 0.5 mm, far below the round-4 plan's 5-10 mm (its 0.3-1 / 2-4 / 5-10 mm classes are replaced by DEC-054). The classes are the median and 90th percentile of 24 tuning PD patients' tip tremor while drawing spirals, checked on 25 test patients (60/24/16 % against 50/40/10); they are a floor, since patients who could not draw on a tablet are missing (LIT PDT-82). This peak is zero-to-peak. EXP-H01 states peak-to-peak (A_pp = 2 sqrt(2) A_rms, human_study_plan.md s3.6), about twice as large for a steady tremor. REQ-USR-002 is now stated in this convention: 0.5 mm peak for full correction (it was 1 mm p-p), the lower edge of the severe class
source: DEC-054; docs/real_data.md (the tremor library); LIT PDT-75, PDT-82
verification: review of every claim; results cards (EXP-R02, AC-R02-04); the classes in writing (EXP-R01, AC-R01-02)
current_estimate: PD tip tremor while drawing is mostly 0.1-0.3 mm; severe (top 10 %) from 0.51 mm, representative 1.72 mm, largest test patient 7.1 mm (CALC on DATA, UCI spirals). No open recording of ET at the pen tip exists; ET waveforms from the hand are scaled to the PD classes (ASSUMPTION)

title: No non-causal inputs to controllers
requirement: Inputs built with non-causal (zero-phase) filters are never given to a controller or estimator; trackers see only the simulated or recorded sensor streams
rationale: The realdata library extracts each tremor waveform with zero-phase band limits (f0 +/- 2 Hz and 2 f0 +/- 2 Hz), which use the future of the recording; it drives the simulated hand only. This is the data-side complement of REQ-CTRL-009 (every command uses only samples available at its tick)
source: DEC-054; docs/real_data.md (the tremor library; how other studies use the library)
verification: code review; library docstrings; the pipeline check of EXP-R05 (AC-R05-02)
current_estimate: The library's docstrings mark every zero-phase filter as for inputs and statistics only, and the HW1 trackers saw only the simulated sensor streams (docs/real_data.md); no automated test checks it yet

title: Dataset licences
requirement: Datasets are used and redistributed only within their licences; results hold statistics only for research-only and non-commercial sources
rationale: UNIPEN (the iUF notice allows research use only; its Zenodo page tags CC BY 4.0, and the stricter terms apply), BRUSH (non-commercial research use), PADS (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and NewHandPD (no licence stated) restrict use; pictures of UNIPEN writing stay in realdata/build/figures_research_only/ (git-ignored). IAM-OnDB, PaHaW and OnHW need registration, an agreement or permission before use (EXP-R06)
verification: the source registry test (realdata/tests); EXP-R04 (AC-R04-01); EXP-R06 (AC-R06-01)
current_estimate: Every dataset used is in the registry with its licence and what may go into results/: statistics only for UNIPEN, BRUSH, PADS and NewHandPD; attributed excerpts for the CC BY sources (UCI, Zenodo); the registry test passes

title: Measured-error page sensor in every tracker simulation
requirement: Every simulation that reports tracker performance also reports it with a measured-error page-sensor model (for now the DeltaPen-class model; the model measured on paper by EXP-R07 once it exists); the ideal sensor only as a labelled bound
rationale: The independent review (R14) and DEC-054. Earlier tracker results assumed 1 kHz, 2 ms and 3 um of white noise (ASSUMPTION). The DeltaPen-class model gives all of DeltaPen's measured 10 ms window error (median 23.6 um, mean 68.3 um, on a Wacom surface, LIT OPT-02) to the sensor, so it is pessimistic. On paper the error is measured on rig R10 (EXP-T04, EXP-J10, DEC-059), and REQ-RVJ-C05 sets its limits
source: DEC-054; docs/real_data.md (the page sensor); LIT OPT-01, OPT-02
verification: results card with both columns (EXP-R02, AC-R02-05); EXP-R07 (AC-R07-01)
current_estimate: The DeltaPen-class model gives 27 um median and 76 um mean per 10 ms window on the tremor-free test notes (against 23.6 and 68.3); with it the results changed by at most 0.1 word and 0.01 mm against the ideal sensor (SIM)

title: Words read by a literal reader
requirement: Words-you-can-read results use a literal reader (no lexicon, no spelling correction, greedy decoding), and report the clean-ink ceiling of the same notes and a 95 % interval over writers
rationale: The independent review (s13) and DEC-054's results card. A reader with a lexicon or a correction step reads words that the ink does not show. The literal reader's decoder still has a language prior from its training text, so even clean notes are not all read: the ceiling row shows it. EXP-R03 checks the reader against people
current_estimate: TrOCR base, literal, chosen on the tuning notes: 6.8 of 10 words on the clean real test notes and 9.5 of 10 on synthetic notes (SIM)

title: Content of the EXP-H01 recordings
requirement: EXP-H01 recordings (with EXP-R01) hold ink on paper over a digitiser (>= 200 points/s, <= 0.05 mm, hover tracked), the pen's IMU with acquisition and availability time stamps, handedness, grip, posture, medication state and device configuration, and participant- and session-level splits
rationale: The independent review (s11) and the gaps of the open data: no open recording of ET at the pen tip; no dataset records availability times; patients' own writing (slower and smaller, adapted to their tremor) is missing from the composed inputs. R11's tablet protocol reports 0.01 mm but is accurate only to about +/-0.25 mm (LIT CON-101), so AC-H01-08 then registers the chain per stroke. It extends REQ-DATA-001 (splits by participant and session) to what the recordings hold
source: DEC-054; docs/real_data.md (proposed requirements); independent review 2026-09-29 s11
current_estimate: Not yet recorded. R11's tablet recorder logs every pen sample the browser receives, with time stamps (AC-T06-04 must show a median >= 200 Hz); the recording pen's IMU runs at 1.92 kHz (docs/measurement_rig.md s4.1)

title: Decisive bench experiment
requirement: Real ink on paper, known reference path, injected housing disturbance, independent metrology of housing, nib and deposited ink; compare cancellation vs powered-neutral vs unpowered
rationale: Brief s17
current_estimate: Protocol drafted

title: Immediate vs lasting benefit
requirement: Assisted performance and unassisted retention/transfer are separate endpoints with separate claims
rationale: Brief s17; COR-20

title: Pencil envelope
requirement: Barrel diameter <= 9.0 mm (8.9 mm target), length <= 170 mm, mass <= 24 g including wiring and margin (20 g target)
rationale: User request for an Apple-Pencil-class form factor (AMF-41: 8.9 x 166 mm, 19.15 g)
verification: EXP-M03 (mass and balance of built pens); EXP-H02 (form factor)
current_estimate: CAD 12.2 g before wiring and margin (Q layout); centre of mass 88 mm from the nib. Proposed P0.2 (DEC-030): 14.6 g including 10 % (CALC)

title: Writing force bypasses the nib
requirement: The user writing force is carried to the paper by a nose skid; the nib force is set by an axial spring at F_c <= 0.14 N (derived from REQ-PNC-003: the loaded stroke is +/-300 um at 0.14 N, +/-277 um at 0.15 N and about +/-180 um at 0.20 N, theta 50 deg, mu 0.15, worst stroke direction); EXP-Q02 shows whether an ink writes well at that force
rationale: Any transverse nib stage must hold N cos(theta) + friction (COR-01); no actuator that fits a 7.9 mm bore holds 0.76 N
verification: EXP-Q01 (skid friction); EXP-Q02 (low-force ink); EXP-Q06 (nib force behind the skid); EXP-H03 (skid feel)
current_estimate: Stage design load 0.170 N per axis behind the skid at the assumed F_c 0.15 N (just above the 0.14 N limit) vs 0.758 N with a conventional nib (docs/pencil_mechanisms.md s2)

title: Pencil stage stroke under load
requirement: Two-axis nib correction >= +/-0.30 mm under the design load over theta 35-75 deg, zero static hold power, first resonance >= 150 Hz
rationale: Tremor of 0.3 mm peak at the nib (REQ-ENV-003 nominal) must fit within the usable stroke
current_estimate: P0.1.2: +/-277 um at the design load (50 deg, nominal parts), 192 Hz; worst case (-20 % parts, 35 deg, mu 0.15, worst direction) 0 um (raw -67 um) under the hardware-study model. Proposed P0.2 (DEC-030): +/-477 um nominal (servo limit +/-300 um), worst case +/-212 um, 213 Hz (CALC, results/opt/hardware.json); still short of +/-0.30 mm in the worst corner, which needs F_c <= 0.10 N (EXP-Q02)

title: Page sensor for capture and guidance
requirement: Page-referenced position at >= 120 Hz with <= 10 ms latency, fused with the IMU between samples, inside the 8.9 mm nose
rationale: Guided mode loses most of its benefit at 30 Hz (0.76 of the no-correction error) and keeps it at >= 120 Hz (0.42)
verification: EXP-S01 on a candidate chip-scale sensor
current_estimate: No part found that fits and meets it (OPT-05 too large; OPT-36 30 fps). With the accelerometer tracker (DEC-025) 120 Hz / 10 ms costs little: tremor-band ratio 0.81 against 0.78 at 1 kHz (SIM); the frozen filter needed 1 kHz (0.998 at 120 Hz)

title: Pencil battery life
requirement: >= 2 h of assisted writing and >= 4 h of recording per charge
rationale: Liftware-class devices run about 1-1.5 h (ACT-16); a pencil used for notes needs a working session
verification: EXP-P01 (power and runtime); EXP-Q03 (cell pulse discharge); EXP-Q05 (driver efficiency)
current_estimate: P0.1.2: 90 mAh cell, recording 4.1 h; assist 0.50 h with 2 x DRV2700 and the real TMAG5170 Hall noise (2.3 um). Proposed P0.2 (DEC-030): assist 2.73 h in the worst 0.3 mm case with an LT8365 charge-recovery drive at 58 V and 2 x DRV5055A4 (CALC, results/opt/hardware.json)

title: Touchdown and lift tails
requirement: Extra ink at touchdown and lift, beyond what a rigid pen draws on the same writing, <= 0.1 mm per stroke; no missing ink
rationale: The skid architecture lets the ball slide up to 0.86 mm at every touchdown and lift with a tilt-range front stop, which harms legibility more than the tremor
current_estimate: Tail ink (within 30 ms of a touchdown or lift) with the tilt-adaptive stop at 0.31 mm and the touchdown feed-forward (DEC-026): 0.005 / 0.008 / 0.000 mm per stroke at 35 / 50 / 75 deg, no missing ink at the transitions (adaptive stop alone 0.14 / 0.11 / 0.00; tilt-range stop 0.35 / 0.81 / 0.42). Met in SIM for touchdown and lift; the all-extra-ink diagnostic (1.15 -> 0.33 -> 0.23 mm, 0.15 with the tuned servo) is dominated by the skid's in-stroke distortion, not the transitions. Open: 1.7 contact transitions per pen-down against 1.2 (short re-contacts after lift-off, bounce family of DEC-011)

title: Bounded guidance from predicted templates
requirement: Guidance toward any template is limited to the stage travel, scaled by the calibrated prediction confidence (ICD s5 rule 5), and must not make a written letter read as another letter in more than 1 % of letters when gated
rationale: Wrong predictions must not rewrite what the user writes
verification: EXP-A02; firmware tests of template rules T1-T8 (docs/ai_guidance.md s7.3)
current_estimate: Stage at its 0.40 mm stop at worst; 2.2 % of letters misread at full authority, 0.3 % gated (pencil model P1)

title: Autocorrect as a derived layer
requirement: Autocorrect changes only derived text layers that cite stroke ids; the original ink and base recognition layer are never modified; every change is visible and reversible; changes require posterior >= 0.9 by default
rationale: Immutable originals and provenance (DEC-017); names and rare words are the failure mode
current_estimate: Word errors 32 % -> 10 % at 7 % recognition errors; <= 0.1 % of correct words changed; names 6-14 % wrongly changed without a personal dictionary

title: Rev H envelope
requirement: Handle grip diameter <= 24 mm and length <= 175 mm; mass <= 80 g without the inertial module and <= 110 g with it
rationale: The user chose a bigger grip (DEC-029); Liftware-class handheld stabilisers weigh about 100 g (ACT-16); pen barrels of 13-21 mm were compared for grip kinetics (HAP-37)
current_estimate: Ø22 x 170 mm; 75.0 g, 103 g with the rear inertial module (92 g with a 10440 cell) (CALC, results/revH/tip_params.json)

title: Rev H tip travel
requirement: Ball travel relative to the handle >= +/-2.5 mm in every direction over theta 35-75 deg with the skid ring on the paper; cross-coupling between axes <= 10 %
rationale: Covers 1-2 mm hand tremor at the tip with margin; travel beyond +/-1.5 mm changed the causal result by < 0.03 in SIM, so +/-2.5 mm leaves room for guidance
current_estimate: +/-3.0 mm usable, 3.5 mm stop at 50 deg (PROPOSED DESIGN); front end closed over 35-75 deg: >= 2.75 mm in every direction with the nozzle >= 0.80 mm above the paper (CALC, DEC-034); never at the limit for 2 mm tremor with perfect knowledge except peaks at 10-12 Hz (SIM)

title: Rev H nose servo
requirement: Closed-loop nose bandwidth (-3 dB) >= 60 Hz with phase margin >= 45 deg, with the real Hall noise; nose force constant >= 0.40 N/sqrt(W) per axis at the magnets
rationale: The tremor band reaches 12 Hz; a servo above 80 Hz changed the causal result by < 0.03 in SIM
current_estimate: Km 0.47 N/sqrt(W) at the magnets (adjoint design); 80 Hz servo ASSUMPTION (CALC, SIM) CONTESTED by DEC-041: an image-method magnetics model gives 0.19 N/sqrt(W) at the magnets (study N, docs/nose_v2.md s4.2); measure first (EXP-N01, AC-N01-03).

title: Rev H power
requirement: Average power while writing <= 0.1 W without the inertial module (>= 20 h of writing per charge on a 750 mAh cell) and <= 0.15 W with it
rationale: All-day use without daily anxiety about charge; the skid carries the load, so the nose only steers
current_estimate: 0.081 W (about 27 h) without the module; module <= 0.051 W, worst case about 17 h (CALC on SIM forces) CONTESTED by DEC-041: with 0.19 N/sqrt(W) the coil loss while writing rises from about 0.004 W to 0.027 W (docs/nose_v2.md s4.2), close to the limit; measure first (EXP-N01).

title: Writing force undisturbed
requirement: Change of the writing (paper-normal) force caused by the nose <= 0.05 N rms while correcting 1 mm tremor
rationale: A tilting rigid nose presses the tip into the paper (architecture A: 0.31-0.71 N rms), which changes ink and feel
current_estimate: Architecture B: none by construction, the refill slides on its 0.15 N spring (SIM)

title: Tremor tracker on real writing
requirement: On recorded writing with 8-12 Hz tremor of >= 1 mm at the tip, ink-error ratio <= 0.8 against the pen with the nose held, with tremor-free writing moved <= 15 um RMS
rationale: The mechanism can remove 76-91 % of tremor up to 2 mm; the tracker decides how much the writer gets
current_estimate: 0.64 / 0.70 / 0.76 at r_rot 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 with 10-13 um false correction (SIM, synthetic writers); nothing at 4-6 Hz

title: Writer stays in charge
requirement: Neither the pen nor the board produces a stroke the writer did not start: nose authority scales with the tracker confidence and is limited to the travel; board force <= 0.4 N and it yields within 0.5 s when the writer resists; a stop is always available
rationale: Agency and safety; learning is shown only without guidance (HAP-01...06)
current_estimate: Board software cap 0.4 N; a determined wrong letter is not overpowered (SIM); nose authority gating by the tracker (DEC-025)

title: Refill front stop follows the nose
requirement: The Rev H refill's front stop follows the nose deflection, or allows at least the usable travel x cot(theta_min) + 0.3 mm of extension
rationale: Tilting the nose by q changes the ball's height by about q x z_p x cot(theta); with a fixed stop 0.3 mm beyond contact the ball touched the paper only 63-73 % of pen-down time under correction (sim2). A fixed long stop lets a free refill follow ordinary pen lifts (DEC-041 item 3), so that option also needs the pen lift or a refill lock
verification: CAD check; EXP-V02 part B; sim2 frontstop stage
current_estimate: Stop that follows the nose (sim2 default): ball in contact 0.908-1.000 of pen-down time, oracle ratio 0.095-0.282; fixed stop 3.2 mm beyond contact: 0.984-1.000, 0.109-0.336; fixed 0.3 mm stop: 0.63-0.73 (SIM, training seeds 300-301). Fixed margin needed: 2.8 mm at 50 deg, 4.6 mm at 35 deg for the 3.0 mm usable travel (CALC). No mechanism designed
trace: DEC-041; results/sim2/verification.json frontstop; docs/sim_v2.md s5.8, s10

title: Heel force cap
requirement: The heel drive's commanded force stays at or below 0.5 N (software cap) and at or below 0.8 x the estimated traction (mu_hat x wheel load); the steered wheel's passive hold across its heading is capped at the same level by a lateral release (the excess turns the wheel toward the push); the physical limit is the static traction (about 0.36-0.73 N)
rationale: Handwriting-guidance devices used 0.43-0.49 N; the desk board 0.4 N; far below ISO/TS 15066 hand limits; the pen always yields to a writer who resists (Rev J envelope)
source: DEC-037; HAP-15; HAP-16; HAP-51; HAP-70; docs/grounded_drive.md s4.4
current_estimate: Commands capped in every SIM run; passive hold up to 0.66 N without the release (test, loops); 95th percentile 0.43-0.50 N and maximum 0.49-0.56 N with it (tuning writers after the test, mu 1.2)

title: The writer always wins
requirement: The drive yields (force to zero within 0.1 s) when the pen is held more than 4 mm off the template for 0.3 s, when the writer's grip force against the drive exceeds 0.5 N for 0.3 s, or on lift; it never keeps pushing against a stalled pen
rationale: Users resent tools that act against their intention; a writer set on 'b' must still write 'b'
source: DEC-037; HAP-22; HAP-23; HAP-62; SIM reversal (writer set on b: 0 % converted)
current_estimate: A writer set on 'b' kept 'b' under every device (push at most 0.37-0.47 N, felt change 0.34-0.48 N at the 95th percentile); the yield rule never had to act, also for a lightly resisting writer (SIM, docs/grounded_drive.md s5.2, s5.3)

title: Passive by default
requirement: In guidance and tremor modes the wheel is steered (and braked) only: it cannot move the pen on its own. The wheel is driven only in an explicit lead-through or autowrite mode the user turns on (DEC-039), and never starts a stroke
rationale: Cobot principle: steering channels the writer's own motion with almost no power (intrinsically passive); Rev J envelope: 'writes for you' only in an explicit mode
current_estimate: Met by the mode logic (SIM); the steer-only wheel drew none of a 'd' bowl with a relaxed hand (docs/grounded_drive.md s5.3)

title: Traction on paper
requirement: Tyre-paper kinetic friction >= 0.6 on the six reference papers at 0.3-0.6 N, dry and at 60 % RH; preload 0.55 N +/- 10 %
rationale: The usable force is mu x wheel load; rubber on paper is 1.05-2.2 for feed rollers, but paper friction tests reproduce only within 24-27 % between labs
current_estimate: Design range 0.6-1.2 (ASSUMPTION); the mean writer gets 0.30 N of traction at mu 0.6 and the weakest 10 % 0.21 N (CALC)

title: Slip detection
requirement: Gross wheel slip is detected within 50 ms (paper sensor against wheel odometry) and the command is lowered; false slip flags fewer than 1 per 10 s of writing
rationale: Slip wastes force and marks the paper; the SIM detector raises many false flags at mode switches. It depends on the page sensor staying in its lens band, which holds only within about +/-1.5 deg of pen roll (DEC-044, REQ-RVJ-N06)
source: DEC-037; AMF-109; SIM (slip flags against true sliding)
current_estimate: Tracing: true sliding < 0.1 % of contact time, yet 3-40 false flags per sentence with the simple rule (SIM); a model-based detector using the tyre deflection is needed. At risk when the pen is rolled, as REQ-RVJ-N06 (CALC, DEC-044); the wheel's odometry could bridge short dropouts

title: Steering speed
requirement: Steering servo bandwidth >= 40 Hz and rate >= 300 rad/s at the wheel
rationale: Letter headings turn at up to 71 rad/s (p90) and 283 rad/s (p99) on the synthetic writers
current_estimate: 0620 B + crown 2:1: about 1570 rad/s no-load at 3.7 V (CALC); SIM servo 40 Hz, limited to 500 rad/s (ASSUMPTION)

title: Roll and tilt tolerance
requirement: The wheel keeps contact over tilts 35-75 deg and pen roll +/-20 deg (spring travel >= 0.75 mm)
rationale: Writers roll the pen; the wheel sits at one azimuth of the heel. Was: spring travel >= 0.54 mm on the Rev H front end (study D); the Rev J ring (11.65 mm) needs 0.75 mm for +/-20 deg of roll (DEC-044)
current_estimate: Rev J (DEC-044): 0.75 mm of spring travel keeps contact to +/-20 deg of roll; the wheel reaches 0.32 / 0.22 / 0.18 mm below the ring's paper plane at 35 / 50 / 75 deg, so its 0.55 N preload always acts (CALC)

title: Front-end size and ink view
requirement: Heel (wheel) contact radius <= 12.0 mm and skid-ring contact radius <= 11.65 mm; front sleeve <= 23.3 mm, flush with the ring, and <= 24 mm where held; the ring stays open 120 deg on top, and the opening carries on 10 mm into the sleeve so the ink stays visible
rationale: The drive must sit outside the swinging nose; the Rev J envelope allows 24 mm where held. Was: heel contact radius <= 9.0 mm and front sleeve <= 18.5 mm at the heel, sized by study D on the Rev H front end; DEC-044 fits the heel to the nose v2 front end (the steering crown sets the 12.0 mm)
source: DEC-037; DEC-036; CALC drive/geometry.py; docs/revJ_plan.md s6
current_estimate: Met at the limits (DEC-044): wheel 12.0 mm, ring 11.65 mm, sleeve front 23.3 mm flush (Rev H's 0.75 mm step would make it 24.8 mm), 24 mm where held with 0.00 mm margin; the C opening carried 10 mm into the sleeve (CALC, PROPOSED DESIGN)
trace: DEC-037; DEC-036; DEC-044; revj/frontend.py; results/revJ/frontend.json; mechanics/cad/revJ_pen.py

title: Power and heat
requirement: Heel drive electrical power (motors and drivers) <= 0.15 W mean in any mode; winding rise < 10 K
rationale: Rev H uses about 0.08 W. The pen's hours per mode are REQ-RVJ-I01, and the page sensor's power is REQ-RVJ-I07 (DEC-045). Was: motors, drivers and paper sensor <= 0.15 W, and the pen still writes >= 8 h with assistance on (the 750 mAh cell must last a school day)
source: DEC-037; DEC-045; AMF-100; docs/revH_concept.md; docs/revJ1_design.md s4.7
current_estimate: Rev J.1 (DEC-045): heel drive 0-2 mW in the steady mode (drivers asleep), 11-26 mW guiding and 103-113 mW leading (84 mW SIM / 0.9 for the fourth gear mesh, plus 10-20 mW of motor drivers, ASSUMPTION); winding rise 5-11 K (CALC). With the PMW3610-class page sensor counted too, 0.105-0.115 W while leading

title: Noise
requirement: Drive noise <= 35 dB(A) at 30 cm while guiding (ASSUMPTION threshold, quiet classroom)
rationale: Two 6 mm motors and watch-scale gears may whine
current_estimate: Unknown (not modelled)

title: Paper must be held
requirement: Instructions and app state that the sheet must be held (other hand, clip or pad) whenever the drive pushes; the drive's force stays below the sheet's holding force
rationale: A loose sheet slides when the drive's reaction exceeds mu_paper-desk x the loads on it
current_estimate: A loose sheet under 1 N slides at 0.25-0.5 N; with the writing hand resting (1 N) and mu 0.5 it holds 1.0 N (CALC; paper-desk mu ASSUMPTION)

title: Clean and replaceable contact
requirement: The tyre and the heel pod can be cleaned or replaced by the user; the pod is sealed against paper dust and ink
rationale: Rolling contacts on paper jam with dust and eraser crumbs (prior art)
current_estimate: Not yet designed or tested

title: Zero force in the air
requirement: Drive torque goes to zero within 20 ms when the wheel load falls below 0.02 N (pen lift); the wheel is pre-steered during lifts
rationale: Pen-up gaps: nothing to push against; dysgraphic writers stop and lift more often
current_estimate: Met in SIM

title: End-cap envelope
requirement: Bench only (DEC-051: no end-cap in the product; it stays a bench comparison against the same mass locked): the end-cap module is <= 26 mm across and <= 45 mm long, <= 45 g, <= 1 W peak and <= 0.3 W average, and the Rev J.1 pen with it fitted stays <= 175 mm and <= 120 g, so that the bench result stands for a module that could be fitted
rationale: Rev J envelope (lead): the pen <= 120 g with every module; a heavier or hungrier end-cap costs grip comfort and battery. Was: the base pen <= 120 g and the pen with the end-cap fitted <= 130 g (provisional; DEC-044 gave 129.2 g with the 43.3 g end-cap); DEC-045's 29.6 g end-cap meets the envelope. Was (DEC-045), a product requirement: 'Rear end-cap <= 26 mm across and <= 45 mm long, <= 45 g, <= 1 W peak and <= 0.3 W average; the pen stays <= 175 mm and <= 120 g with the end-cap fitted'
verification: CAD check; weighing (EXP-K01); EXP-K01 power log; EXP-J09 (acceptance of the masses)
current_estimate: Rev J.1 (DEC-045): end-cap Ø26 x 21 mm, 29.6 g (9 mm tungsten slug, 17.3 g); 0.082 W average in the design model and 0.028 W in the SIM test runs (peak not recomputed; study K's 45 g end-cap 1.0 W). Pen 143.9 mm and 84.3 g base; 161.9 mm and 112.7 g with the end-cap, centre of mass 102.5 mm from the tip (CALC): 7.3 g under 120 g
trace: DEC-038; DEC-044; DEC-045; results/endcap/endcap_study.json; results/revJ1/budgets.json; results/revJ1/endcap.json

title: End-cap tremor benefit
requirement: Bench only (DEC-051): with the nose on, on a hand simulant, the end-cap adds >= 10 % further reduction of the ink error at 8-12 Hz and 1-2 mm at the measured grip split (>= 5 % at the other splits) and never raises it on average; a return to the product is judged by REQ-WP-001
rationale: Pre-declared rule R-T1 of study K; same bar as DEC-033 for the Rev H module. Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'With the nose on, on a hand simulant, the end-cap adds >= 10 % further reduction of the ink error at 8-12 Hz and 1-2 mm at the measured grip split (>= 5 % at the other splits) and never raises it on average'. Product entry for any added device is now REQ-WP-001 (>= 10 % against the same pen with the device locked, at three grip strengths, coverage kept)
source: DEC-038; DEC-051; DEC-033; study K rule R-T1
verification: EXP-K02 (with EXP-I06); EXP-J16 (the Rev J.1 end-cap); EXP-T16 (rig R14, three grip strengths)
current_estimate: +8 / +18 / +20 % at r_rot 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 on top of the Rev H nose (seed spread +4 to +25 %); no split worse on average (SIM, H1, synthetic writers, test seeds 200-203); not re-run with nose v2. Rev J.1 end-cap (29.6 g, DEC-045): +5.6 / +16.8 / +18.3 % (SIM, same model and test seeds; rule R-T1 passes by 0.6 points at 0.3)

title: Active beats its own weight
requirement: Bench only (DEC-051): on the bench the active end-cap is compared with the same mass fixed in the end-cap and must beat it by >= 5 points of further reduction at the measured grip split; the product fits neither, and a return is judged by REQ-WP-001
rationale: The weight alone gives part of the benefit in SIM; an active part costs power and complexity. Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'An active end-cap is fitted only if it beats the same mass fixed in the end-cap by >= 5 points of further reduction at the measured grip split; otherwise fit the weight or nothing'. REQ-WP-001's gate (>= 10 % over the device locked, at every grip strength, coverage kept) is stricter; AC-T16-01, which asked it as a hypothesis on this requirement, is now REQ-WP-001's criterion
verification: EXP-K02; EXP-K03; EXP-J16; EXP-T16 (rig R14, three grip strengths)
current_estimate: The same 45 g fixed: +17 / +12 / +4 %, so the motion adds -9 / +6 / +16 points at r_rot 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7; the fixed weight makes 8 / 29 / 42 % of the hard cases worse than the nose alone, the moving slug 4 / 12 / 4 % (SIM). Rev J.1 end-cap (29.6 g, DEC-045): the same mass fixed +12.6 / +11.1 / +6.7 %, so the motion adds -7.0 / +5.7 / +11.6 points (SIM)

title: No writing claim for inertia
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-051: the pen carries no end-cap. If one returns through REQ-WP-001, no product text, mode or app screen may claim that it moves, steers or writes letters; it is described as a steadier and a cue
rationale: SIM: no end-cap design reaches the 2 mm 'can write' line at 1-3 Hz. Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'No product text, mode or app screen may claim that the end-cap moves, steers or writes letters; the end-cap is described as a steadier and a cue'
source: DEC-038; DEC-051; study K s6 (rule R-S1)
current_estimate: Largest ink shift at 1-3 Hz: reaction mass 0.21 mm, CMG 1.06 mm, against 2 mm to write (SIM)

title: Cue side effect
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-051: the pen carries no end-cap. If one returns through REQ-WP-001, any end-cap cue given while the ball is on the paper keeps the ink jitter <= 30 um RMS; otherwise cues are given only in pauses or with the pen lifted
rationale: Pre-declared rule R-C1; a cue that moves the ink defeats the pen. Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'Any end-cap cue given while the ball is on the paper keeps the ink jitter <= 30 um RMS; otherwise cues are given only in pauses or with the pen lifted'. The pen's cue is now an LRA tick (DEC-056; EXP-S13)
source: DEC-038; DEC-051; study K s8 (rule R-C1)
current_estimate: A 0.5 N, 40 + 80 Hz cue moves the ink 186 um RMS while writing (116-239 um over the grip splits); 76 um at 0.25 N; 31 um at 75 Hz (SIM): cues belong in pauses

title: Cue validated in the target users
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-051: the pen carries no end-cap. If one returns through REQ-WP-001, a directional end-cap cue is shipped only if >= 90 % of directions are named correctly by writers with ET and with PD (with tremor) in EXP-K05
rationale: Pseudo-force direction was near chance on sides with tremor in the only patient study found (preprint). Was (DEC-038), a product requirement: 'A directional cue is shipped only if >= 90 % of directions are named correctly by writers with ET and with PD (with tremor) in EXP-K05'
current_estimate: Healthy adults 93-99 % (HAP-82, HAP-84, HAP-85); tremor sides near chance (PDT-39, preprint)

title: Rotor safety (only if a rotor is fitted)
requirement: Applies to the CMG research module (no rotor in the product, DEC-038): stored rotor energy <= 3 J; a burst is contained by the end-cap; the rotor stops within 2 s after a fall is detected; balance grade G1 or better (G0.4 is the gyroscope class); spin-up <= 10 s
rationale: A spinning tungsten disc in a hand-held pen is a new hazard (Rev J plan s6). REQ-WP-010 (DEC-051) asks more of any gyroscope in the tail tests (EXP-W14): <= 2 J and a burst excluded by design (stress margin >= 3, over-speed trip); this requirement keeps its lines for the end-cap's CMG research module
current_estimate: CMG end-cap: 3.0 J (at the cap), spin-up 8.1 s, 466 Hz tone, centre stress 3.9 MPa against >= 724 MPa (factor 184), imbalance 0.16 N at G2.5 and 0.026 N at G0.4 (CALC); stop time 2 s is a target (ASSUMPTION)

title: Battery with the end-cap
requirement: Superseded for the product by DEC-051: the pen carries no end-cap, so REQ-RVJ-I01 has no end-cap row. If one returns through REQ-WP-001: with it fitted and active only while a tremor line is detected, >= 8 h of steady writing up to 1 mm tremor at the end-cap's measured duty and >= 6 h at its design power
rationale: One set of battery targets for every mode (docs/revJ1_design.md s4.7); the id is kept so that references still resolve. Was: >= 8 h of writing per charge with the end-cap active (Rev J envelope). Was (DEC-045): 'Folded into REQ-RVJ-I01 by DEC-045 as its end-cap row: with the end-cap fitted and active only while a tremor line is detected, >= 8 h of steady writing up to 1 mm tremor at the end-cap's measured duty and >= 6 h at its design power'
source: DEC-038; DEC-051; DEC-045; docs/revJ_plan.md s6; docs/revJ1_design.md s4.7
verification: EXP-K01 power log with the nose on (AC-K01-05)
current_estimate: Rev J.1 (DEC-045), steady writing at 1 mm tremor with the end-cap active: 7.7-8.6 h at the end-cap's SIM power (27.6 mW; 8.6 h only with the typical electronics) and 6.4-7.1 h at its design power (82 mW) (CALC, SIM). Rev J (DEC-044): 4.3-6.6 h

title: Non-magnetic mass near the sensors
requirement: Tungsten parts within 20 mm of a Hall sensor or coil are a non-magnetic grade (W-Ni-Cu class)
rationale: W-Ni-Fe heavy alloys are weakly ferromagnetic and would bias the Hall sensors and the coils
current_estimate: ET95NM relative permeability <= 1.05 (AMF-49); INERMET grades paramagnetic (AMF-125)

title: Guaranteed tip travel
requirement: Ball travel relative to the handle >= 6.0 mm in every direction over 35-75 deg of tilt with the skid ring on the paper
rationale: Autowrite of 2.5 mm letters needs 4.1 mm for the worst tuning writer, plus 1 mm kept free for tremor (CALC, docs/nose_v2.md s2); also covers 3 mm letters; the 100 ms of delayed ink it also allowed for was dropped by DEC-042
current_estimate: Rev J integrated layout (DEC-044): 6.00 mm guaranteed and 6.57 mm nominal at 50 deg (nose angle raised to 0.0859 rad so that the larger heel ring keeps 6.0 mm at 75 deg); skid ring 11.65 mm, heel wheel 12.0 mm; refill slide 26.6 mm (CALC)

title: Nose force and bandwidth
requirement: Force constant at the tip >= 0.85 x the design value (0.099 N/sqrt(W) per axis, so >= 0.084) over the whole travel; closed-loop bandwidth >= 60 Hz; first parasitic mode >= 240 Hz
rationale: The design's power and heat margins rest on Km; the magnetics are an upper bound (image method, CALC, docs/nose_v2.md s4.2); 240 Hz is 3 x the 80 Hz servo
verification: EXP-N01; EXP-N03; study B's coupon and nib on rigs R12 and R13: EXP-T07, T08, T10
current_estimate: 0.66 N/sqrt(W) at the magnets, 0.099 N/sqrt(W) at the tip (image-method magnetics, an upper bound); first parasitic mode 788 Hz; 80 Hz servo used in SIM (CALC)

title: Heat
requirement: Coil temperature rise <= 20 K while autowriting with 1 mm tremor for 30 min; held surfaces <= 43 C absolute in a rated 30 C room (a 13 K rise), with 41 C as the design target, checked at the web over the coil plate (the rule of REQ-THM-001)
rationale: Skin contact: ECMA-287 Table 5.2 gives 43 C for continuously held parts, and its B.5 lets the maker rate a warmer room (LIT AMF-35); under IEC 60601-1, 41 C needs no justification (LIT AMF-34). With 2 mm tremor the coil loss doubles, so such texts must stay short. Was: 'skin surface <= 41 C at the web over the coil plate in a 30 C room' (DEC-044); before that 'grip surface <= 41 C' with no room named
verification: EXP-N04; EXP-J05; EXP-J13; EXP-T15 (rig R13, the balanced nib with the governor)
current_estimate: Rev J.1 (DEC-045), 0.1 mm graphite sheet in the shell wall (+0.21 g): the web 35.9 C at 1 mm tremor in a 30 C room, coil rise 8.5-8.7 K; autowrite with 2 mm tremor 43.7 C and 20.0 K: short texts, or a firmware cap at 0.39 W of coil loss (the coils may dissipate 0.395 W for 43 C and 0.334 W for 41 C) (CALC, fin model). At 2 x study N's coil power the web reaches 42.1 C at 1 mm tremor, at 5 x 63.8 C. Suspended by DEC-046 until study B and EXP-J17: with the refill spring's static side load (1.6 W at 50 deg, REQ-RVJ-N10) the coil would settle 162 K above the room, and at sim2's 2.68 W on the paper it passes 120 C after about 22 s (CALC on SIM; 100 K/W and 0.5 J/K ASSUMPTION)
trace: DEC-036; DEC-044; DEC-045; results/nose2/nose2.json; revj1/thermal.py; results/revJ1/budgets.json; DEC-046; results/sim2j/power_split.json

title: Pen lift
requirement: The pen lifts the ball >= 0.3 mm off the paper and lowers it within 8 ms of the command, holds either state with no power, >= 1e7 cycles
rationale: Strokes stay separate at 50-70 deg (a free refill follows ordinary pen lifts, DEC-041 item 3); autowrite and delayed ink need it (docs/nose_v2.md s2, s5)
verification: EXP-N05; EXP-T11 (rig R13, the loaded nib)
current_estimate: 0.5 mm lift, 5 ms switching (8 ms command to contact in SIM), 17 mJ per cycle, 0.07 W while autowriting, no holding power (electro-permanent brake and bistable latch) (CALC on ASSUMPTION inputs); freedom-to-operate review of PAT-01 open

title: Refill force element
requirement: Ink force along the refill 0.15 N +/- 20 % over the whole refill slide (26.6 mm; tendon travel 27.4 mm), never above 0.2 N along the refill; no fatigue failure within 1e8 small cycles
rationale: Stock constant-force springs are rated 2 500-25 000 cycles (MFR AMF-144); tremor stabilisation cycles the slide about 29 000 times per hour; the ball's drag is the nose's largest load. The slide was 24.4 mm with study N's front end; DEC-044's larger ring makes it 26.6 mm
verification: EXP-N06; EXP-J06; EXP-T02 (rig R9: the lowest reliable ink force)
current_estimate: Rev J (DEC-044): spiral spring of 301 full-hard strip, 38 um x 2.6 x 139 mm, in the drum: 0.12-0.18 N along the refill over the 27.4 mm tendon travel, 0.19-0.21 N normal at the ball; Goodman safety factor 1.73 at 1e8 small cycles (+/-1.3 mm) and 1.30 at full travel (CALC; fatigue strength LIT AMF-20 with 0.8 ASSUMPTION); a 0.3 N ink force raised the coil loss 2.4-fold (SIM)

title: Page sensor
requirement: Handle position on the page at >= 1 kHz, <= 2 ms latency, <= 10 um rms, while writing at 35-75 deg of tilt and pen roll +/-20 deg, with the lens height within the sensor's working band
rationale: Autowrite's estimator and the SIM results assume it; with a 120 Hz, 10 ms sensor the autowrite ink error more than doubles (72 against 30 um); the heel drive uses it to detect slip (DEC-037). Was: 35-75 deg of tilt, no roll range named; writers roll the pen (REQ-DRV-007: +/-20 deg)
verification: EXP-N07; EXP-J04; EXP-J10; EXP-T04 and EXP-T05 (rig R10, the bare sensor)
current_estimate: Rev J (DEC-044): folded optics beside the heel wheel; lens 2.23-2.45 mm above the paper over 35-75 deg with no roll, inside the 2.2-2.6 mm band (MFR OPT-54); 2.06-2.74 mm at +/-5 deg and 1.59-4.11 mm at +/-20 deg of roll, so the band holds only within about +/-1.5 deg (CALC): at risk. SIM assumed 1 kHz, 2 ms, 3 um noise; no part tested. Rev J.1 (DEC-045): a PMW3610-class die in the same place and optics, on in every mode; its frame rate and accuracy on paper are not stated (MFR OPT-61): EXP-J10; a PMW3360-class die stays the fallback for autowrite
trace: DEC-036; DEC-044; DEC-045; nose2/autowrite.py; results/revJ/frontend.json; results/revJ1/budgets.json

title: Autowrite is a mode the user turns on
requirement: The pen draws letters on its own only in an explicit autowrite mode the user turns on, and only text the user accepted (typed, dictated, copied in the app, or a suggestion accepted with one action; DEC-049, DEC-056), in the user's own style, at up to 3 mm of tremor (DEC-049; sim2's peak at the hand); the app and the stroke record label that text as pen-written; it writes through a plan that starts a letter only when all of it fits within reach (REQ-CTRL-014); it follows the user's sweep and waits when the user slows; it sets the sweep speed per line and cues the user; it lifts the ball and stops drawing when the text leaves its reach; it never pushes the hand with the nose (the heel drive may lead a relaxed hand at gross scale, DEC-037); assistance modes never start a stroke
rationale: docs/revJ_plan.md s6; HAP-62 (users were frustrated when a handheld robot disobeyed); ACT-100 (Origin retracts when out of bounds). Amends REQ-RVH-007 for this mode (DEC-039). DEC-049 widens the mode to accepted text (study S's accepted suggestions) and to 3 mm of tremor, with the text labelled pen-written; DEC-056 (f) feeds it through the writing plan with letter admission and a reach gate (REQ-CTRL-014). At 3 mm peak at the hand the ordinary pen's ink error was 1.38-1.55 mm rms (sim2), DEC-054's severe class at the tip. Was (DEC-039): 'The pen draws letters on its own only in an explicit autowrite mode the user turns on, and only a known text (typed, dictated or copied in the app) in the user's own style; it follows the user's sweep and waits when the user slows; it sets the sweep speed per line and cues the user; it lifts the ball and stops drawing when the text leaves its reach; it never pushes the hand with the nose (the heel drive may lead a relaxed hand at gross scale, DEC-037); assistance modes never start a stroke'
verification: design review; EXP-N09 (AC-N09-02); EXP-S19 (the plan on the bench); EXP-S18 (accepted suggestions, one action)
current_estimate: In SIM the pen followed the sweep and waited: an uneven sweep (+/-30 %) or a drifting hand (+/-1 mm) left the ink at 30-31 um; one of six test writers needed a slower sweep for its line (post hoc) (docs/nose_v2.md s5.3, s5.5). DEC-049 (sim2, 6 test writers, 3 mm peak at the hand, 5 and 8 Hz): letters read 82 / 88 %, words (after autocorrect) 80 / 97 %, ink 67 / 83 um from the planned letters; the nose used 6.55 of its 6.57 mm. Study S (kinematics only): an accepted word at a 3 mm x-height is written in full in 95 % of cases at +/-6 mm with the hand advancing, 23 % at +/-4 mm, 2 % with a still hand
trace: DEC-039; DEC-049; DEC-056; nose2/autowrite.py; nose2/planner.py; ai3/complete_plan.py; ai3/layers.py; results/sim2j/autowrite.json

title: Autowrite legibility (SIM gate before hardware)
